description: See sine and cosine as the vertical and horizontal parts of a point on a circle of radius 1, with matching bars and graphs.

educational.topic: Sine and cosine on the unit circle
learningObjectives: Explain sine as the vertical part and cosine as the horizontal part of a point on a circle
Predict the sign of sine and cosine in each quarter of the circle
Convert between degrees and radians for key angles
prerequisites: Right triangles: hypotenuse, opposite and adjacent sides

keyQuestions: Why can sine never be larger than 1 on the unit circle?
Where are sine and cosine equal?
How is the cosine graph related to the sine graph?
commonMisconceptions: Sine is the horizontal part (sine is vertical, cosine is horizontal)
assessmentOpportunities: The student states that cos 90 degrees = 0 and sin 90 degrees = 1 and shows why on the circle.
The student predicts both signs for an angle such as 225 degrees before checking.
The student converts 180 degrees to pi radians.
